title: What belongs on an underground map?
instruction: A model for travelling by underground. What do you keep in it and what do you leave out?

items.why: Without stations you don't know where to get on and off.
That tells you where a line will take you.
Without the changes you can't plan a journey on two lines.

items.text: The order of stations on a line
items.why: You know how many stops to go and where to get off.
They are no use to you underground.

items.text: The exact length of the tunnel in metres
items.why: For the journey, the order of the stations is enough.

items.text: The colour of the house fronts
items.why: You can't see them from the underground.

items.text: The names of shops by the exit
items.why: You don't need them to travel by underground. They belong on a map of the area.

debrief: A good model keeps only what you need for the task. For an underground journey, stations, lines and changes are enough. Streets, lengths and shops would just clutter the map.
